mode achieved: static review of the final snapshot (task12-final) plus light probes from lanes/cleanup after cmp against the snapshot (all compared files identical): read all 18 files of e2e/web, the three Maestro flows, playwright.config.ts, package.json, check.yml, CONTRIBUTING.md, eslint.config.js, eslint-rules/restrictions.js, scripts verify.mjs, canary.mjs, canaries.mjs, check-trace.mjs, mutation.mjs, native-gate.mjs, check-web-release.mjs, check-language.mjs (rules part), test-floor.json, stryker.config.json and the tests check-trace.test.mjs, canary.test.mjs, canaries.test.mjs, verify.cli.test.mjs (verify.test.mjs and verify.record.test.mjs by grep); ran 11 probes (4 eslint --stdin-filename, 1 check-language, check-trace titlesOf and run, verify treeOf and commitOf, mutation planOf, git in the lanes) and read the lane's real reports/e2e.json; ran no gate, Jest, Playwright, Stryker, expo or Maestro
verdict: 12 of 14 round-1 keys closed, 2 not closed (the tree hash is unknown where verify runs; the native layout is still checked only by the CSS emulation); 1 regression, 3 new majors, 3 nits. The gate system is now strong; its holes are inverted tests, browser specs outside the trace, and helper-only changes outside the PR mutation scope.

## Regressions

🟡 major  The trace gate now ignores every browser spec, so D-19 is traced only by tests that never run in a browser
- key: scripts/check-trace.mjs#browser-specs-untraced
- where: scripts/check-trace.mjs:121 (titles only from src/screens/<id> and e2e/web/<id>); e2e/web holds no screen folder (all 18 files at its root); scripts/check-trace.test.mjs:160 pins `e2e/web/narrow.spec.ts` as "a spec of no screen"; CONTRIBUTING.md:143-146; src/screens/24-project-overview/contract.yaml:9
- why: round 1's fix paired the per-screen scope with "move the screen 24 specs into e2e/web/24-project-overview/"; the scope landed, the move did not. Probe (node import of run() from check-trace.mjs, 2026-10-10): the real lane tree and a tree holding src/screens with an empty e2e/web both return 0 with "9 requirement codes, each named by a running test of its own screen". The 11 coded browser titles (narrow.spec.ts, 8 declarations giving 36 tests per browser, and controls.pages.spec.ts:24, :58, :83 for BR-32, OVW-01, OVW-05) count for nothing. D-19 now rests on StatusCard.test.native.tsx:213, :231 and Screen.test.native.tsx:162, which run on the iOS and Android Jest projects only (CONTRIBUTING.md:154-155), while FE-23's defect was screen 24 in a phone browser.
- trigger: plan C adds screen 26 with D-19 in its contract and one `.test.native.tsx` titled D-19; no browser spec measures it at 360 px; gate:trace prints that every code is traced; the web phone layout of screen 26 ships untested, the FE-23 failure again.
- guard-bypass: the trace's own test asserts that a root spec counts for nothing; gate:web's floor counts the tests of all specs together, so it never asks for a spec of a given screen; the trace canary plants only a contract that no test names.
- fix: move the specs that prove screen 24 (narrow, shape, states, controls, controls.pages, contract) into e2e/web/24-project-overview/ with their relative imports, as CONTRIBUTING.md:146 already requires; let contract.yaml list the codes a browser must prove (for example `web: [D-19, OVW-01]`) and make check-trace require each of them in a spec under e2e/web/<screen>/, with a check-trace.test.mjs case and a canary.
- approach-changing: no, a file move plus one optional contract field
- design: yes, a per-layer requirement list in the contract

## New findings

🟡 major  The tree hash is "unknown" wherever pnpm verify runs, so the final report binds no row to a tree and says its rows are not on one tree
- key: scripts/verify.mjs#tree-unknown-in-lanes
- where: scripts/verify.mjs:101-120 (treeOf), :122-128 (commitOf), :224 and :235 (All rows on one tree); scripts/verify.test.mjs:282-286; plan Task 14 Step 1 runs pnpm verify in the main lane; CLAUDE.md runs it in ~/metis-run/verify
- why: treeOf asks git for the file list, and the lanes and the verify copy are copies without .git. Probe (2026-10-10): in lanes/cleanup/apps/metis, which holds this tree's gate reports (reports/e2e.json, jest.json), `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z -- . ../../brand` exits 128, treeOf returns `unknown (git could not list the files)` and commitOf returns `none`; `git rev-parse` in ~/metis-run/verify prints "fatal: not a git repository". Every row of the Task 14 report will carry the same unknown tree, and render() then prints `All rows on one tree: no`, a claim that the rows ran on different trees. The round-1 trigger still reproduces: edit a file after the run, append a rerun with --only, and verify.md cannot show that the trees differ.
- trigger: Task 14 runs pnpm verify in lanes/cleanup; Task 15 fixes a finding and appends a rerun; verify.md shows `Tree: unknown` on every row and "All rows on one tree: no"; the owner's package cites it and cannot match it to the tree Task 16 merges into the repo.
- guard-bypass: verify.test.mjs:282-286 pins unknown as the designed result off git, and verify.cli.test.mjs runs every case in a temp folder without git, so no test needs a known tree; the lanes are made by copying the repo without .git.
- fix: run `git init -q` at the root of each lane and of ~/metis-run/verify when it is made (the copies carry the .gitignore files, so `ls-files -co --exclude-standard` lists the same files as the repo, which has no commit either, and the lane hash equals the repo hash after the merge); print `All rows on one tree: unknown` when any row is unknown; and print a warning line above the table, or exit 1 on a full run, when the tree is unknown, so the final record cannot lose it silently.
- approach-changing: no, the run copies gain a throwaway .git and render gains one branch

🟡 major  An inverted test passes every gate: Playwright test.fail, Jest test.failing and node:test t.skip or t.todo get through lint, and verify counts an expected failure as a pass
- key: eslint-rules/restrictions.js#inverted-tests
- where: eslint-rules/restrictions.js:53-72 (MODIFIER is only, skip, todo, fixme; node:test options only); scripts/verify.mjs:58-71 (gate:web passed is stats.expected); scripts/check-trace.mjs:48-59 (a bare body call counts only for skip and fixme); CONTRIBUTING.md:136-139
- why: probes (lane eslint with --stdin-filename, 2026-10-10): an e2e spec whose D-19 test calls `test.fail()` in its body, plus a `test.fail('D-19 ...', body)` declaration: exit 0; a Jest `test.failing('OVW-01 ...')` in src/core: exit 0; a node:test file whose tests call `t.skip()` and `t.todo()`: exit 0. titlesOf counts the body-level test.fail test as a running test (returned ["D-19 360 px en: one column"]). Playwright documents test.fail as the way "to acknowledge that some functionality is broken until it is fixed" [Source: node_modules/playwright/types/test.d.ts:5195-5250], and its JSON report counts such a run in stats.expected: the lane's reports/e2e.json has expected 208, of which 8 runs have expectedStatus "failed" (test.spec.ts:113, :123, :132, :142 on both browsers, all legitimate today). Jest reports a test.failing test that throws as a success [Source: node_modules/jest-circus/build/run.js:334-339]. gate:tooling has no skip count at all. A broken requirement can be parked green, the same parking the rule bans for skip and fixme.
- trigger: a D-19 360 px test turns red on WebKit after a layout change; the developer adds `test.fail(browserName === 'webkit', 'known')` as the Playwright docs suggest; gate:lint exits 0, gate:web reads "208 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped", and the WebKit phone layout stays broken.
- guard-bypass: the disabled-test selector lists only, skip, todo and fixme; verify reads the stats only, where an expected failure is a pass; the floor counts it as a passed test.
- fix: add fail and failing to MODIFIER and allow test.fail only in e2e/web/test.spec.ts through an override block for that file; ban `.skip()` and `.todo()` calls on the context parameter of a node:test callback; in verify, count the Playwright tests whose expectedStatus is "failed" from the report's suites and turn gate:web RED when that count differs from a committed number (8 today); in check-trace treat a body-level test.fail() like a bare skip; add a canary that plants a test.failing in a src test file.
- approach-changing: no, selectors and one count
- design: yes, an allow-list for the guard's self-tests and an expected-failure count in verify

🟡 major  On a pull request, a change to a shared test helper mutates nothing and the mutation row reads green
- key: scripts/mutation.mjs#helpers-out-of-scope
- where: scripts/mutation.mjs:30-71 (sourcesOf, COVERS, planOf); scripts/verify.mjs:28 and :193-198; CONTRIBUTING.md:216-219; .github/workflows/check.yml:53
- why: the PR scope is the changed sources plus "the source beside each changed test", and a shared helper has no source beside it. Probe (node import of planOf with stryker.config.json's mutate globs, 2026-10-10): a diff holding only src/design-system/tokens.test.helper.ts (mocked into 35 test files), src/spy.test.helper.ts (11 files), src/mocks/server.test.helper.ts or src/window.test.setup.ts each returns scope { files: 0, reason: "no changed source file since origin/main" }, while a diff of src/design-system/Row.test.native.tsx mutates src/design-system/Row.tsx. verify then writes a green row "0 files: no changed source file since origin/main". A helper change can weaken the assertions of many files at once, which is what mutation testing exists to catch, and only the full run on a Mac would show the survivors.
- trigger: a refactor PR rewrites rowsOf or looksOf in src/spy.test.helper.ts so it reads fewer props; the 11 files that use it still pass; gate:mutation on the PR mutates 0 files and is green; the weakened tests merge.
- guard-bypass: COVERS (mutation.mjs:44) maps only the dictionary registry test; sourcesOf maps a helper to file names that do not exist, or to tokens.ts, which mutate excludes; a 0-file scope is green by design (verify.mjs:28).
- fix: in planOf, for a changed `*.test.helper.*`, `*.test.setup.*` or jest.config.js, add the sources of every test file that imports it (the TypeScript parser check-trace.mjs already uses can read the imports); when that set is too large for the CI budget, write the row as partial with the reason "a shared test helper changed: run gate:mutation on a Mac and append"; add one mutation.test.mjs case per helper kind.
- approach-changing: no, the scope gains an importer lookup
- design: yes, an importer-based scope for shared test code

💭 nit  The "menu closes" check has no positive twin, so a changed role makes it pass with the menu still open
- key: e2e/web/routes.spec.ts#menu-absence-unproven
- where: e2e/web/routes.spec.ts:66-74; CONTRIBUTING.md:128-134; the role is set at src/design-system/Menu.tsx:22
- why: the test opens the menu and clicks its item by testID, then asserts that `getByRole('menu')` has count 0; no e2e line ever matches `getByRole('menu')` on the open menu (grep of e2e/web: the absence line only). If Menu's role changes, the absence assertion passes with the menu drawn, against the convention of CONTRIBUTING.md:128.
- fix: `await expect(page.getByRole('menu')).toBeVisible()` right after the switcher click, the same expression as the absence check.
- approach-changing: no

💭 nit  The test floor is raised by hand, so a later loss of up to the accumulated slack goes unseen
- key: scripts/test-floor.json#floor-drifts
- where: scripts/test-floor.json (`{ "unit": 2663, "web": 160 }`); scripts/verify.mjs:30-40; CONTRIBUTING.md:208-209
- why: the floor holds round 1's counts while this tree runs 2864 Jest tests and 208 browser runs (brief), so today 201 Jest tests or 48 browser runs can vanish under a green row. Task 14 Step 1 resets it once; after that every added test widens the slack again, because nothing asks for the raise.
- fix: make the floor an exact count: the row is RED when passed differs from the floor, with the reason "passed N, floor M: update scripts/test-floor.json", so the change that adds or removes tests updates the file in the same diff.
- approach-changing: no

💭 nit  Lint does not see a demo id typed inside a path, so "paths come from e2e/web/paths.ts" is a reviewer-only rule
- key: eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js#ids-in-paths
- where: CONTRIBUTING.md:55-60; eslint-rules/no-restated-literals.js (whole-string equality); src/mocks/fixtures/ids.ts:2-8
- why: probe (lane eslint, --stdin-filename e2e/web/p7.spec.ts, 2026-10-10): 'Open menu' and 'Northwind Furniture Co.' are flagged, while `page.goto('/w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview')` on the next line, built from IDS.workspace and IDS.meridian, is not. No e2e line types a path or an id today (grep: only `page.goto('/')`), so nothing is wrong yet; round 1 counted 13 such lines in 11 files, and nothing stops the next spec from going back.
- fix: in no-restated-literals, also report a string or template part that holds a value of IDS as a whole path segment.
- approach-changing: no
